CODE DERIVATION: data/wang_2015_donation_decision.py melts the S1 workbook's named columns with ITEM_MAP {distress->distress, sympthy->sympathy, Q4WTC->wtc_amount} -- a name-preserving rename, no positional step; the codes are also self-describing. mapping_basis=paper_explicit because the words come from the paper's Methods (the S1 headers are bare names carrying no wording). VERIFIED against the paper's own published cell statistics, route 1 + route 2 -- see verify_wang_2015_donation_decision.R. OPTIONS: option_text is blank for every row by design. The paper states distress and sympathy were rated 'on a 7-point scale (ranging from "not at all" to "very much")' but names no intermediate labels, and the stored codes are EIGHT values 0-7 (S1 and the live table agree: distress 0:10 1:34 2:27 3:57 4:52 5:87 6:36 7:68; sympathy 0:2 1:22 2:14 3:40 4:44 5:53 6:51 7:145), so which code carries 'not at all' cannot be settled and neither anchor was assigned. wtc_amount is an open donation amount out of 100 (stored by tens), not a labelled option set. Nothing padded with its own number. INSTRUCTIONS blank: the paper describes the leukemia vignette ('All participants read about a sick child [eight children] with leukemia whose life is [lives are] in danger...') but does not reproduce the stimulus text, so there is no literal instruction text to transcribe. LANGUAGE: mixed administration -- 208 Chinese undergraduates read a Chinese version, 163 American students an English one. The paper supplies only English wording, presenting the Chinese donation question as 'Imagine you had one hundred Yuan (about 15 $), how much (if any) of it would you donate...' against the U.S. 'one hundred dollars' version; the U.S. English is shipped verbatim in item_text. source_ref: Wang YN (2016) PLOS ONE 11(1):e0146050 doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0146050 (Study 1 Measures; Table 1) and its S1 Dataset (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0146050.s001, SPSS, no labels); Wood AM, Linley PA, Maltby J, Baliousis M, Joseph S (2008) J Counseling Psychology 55(3):385-399 doi:10.1037/0022-0167.55.3.385, Authenticity Scale appendix, read from the verbatim reproduction at https://cic.edu/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Authenticity-Scale.pdf and cross-checked against https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7838489/ ; IRW processing script data/wang_2016_authenticity_relationship.py
note: PASS with caveats. (1) Administered language: Study 1's 104 Beijing-area college students completed paper-and-pencil questionnaires and 'All questionnaires were presented in their Chinese versions. The English scales were translated into Chinese ... by a native Chinese speaker' (Wang 2016, Study 1 Measures). The administered Chinese wording is not recoverable within scope: the only deposit files are the three SPSS datasets S1/S2/S3, and s001.sav carries NO variable labels and NO value labels at all (checked with pyreadstat: 55 columns, every column_names_to_labels entry None except four Zscore() autolabels; variable_value_labels == {}); there is no questionnaire supplement. Hence the fallback -- English in the base fields, _translated columns empty, language=Chinese. (2) text_source=translated_substitute / translation_source=official_instrument_english: the shipped words are Wood et al.'s (2008) own English for AS items 1, 8, 9 and 11, read from a verbatim reproduction of the scale appendix (cic.edu/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Authenticity-Scale.pdf, which prints all 12 items, the 1-7 'does not describe me at all'/'describes me very well' anchors and the scoring key 'Total items 1, 8, 9, and 11 for Authentic Living') and cross-checked item by item against Nartova-Bochaver et al., 'The Authenticity Scale: Validation in Russian Culture' (Front. Psychol., PMC7838489), which quotes the same four originals verbatim while describing their negative rewording. DEVIATIONS, disclosed: the cic.edu reproduction contains two obvious typos, 'I am true to myself I most situations' and (item 7, not shipped) 'I fell as if'; the shipped item 9 reads 'in most situations', which is the form PMC7838489 quotes. The two sources also differ on one comma -- cic.edu prints 'I think it is better to be yourself, than to be popular', PMC7838489 'to be yourself than to be popular'; the comma form ships. (3) Anchors: the study replaced Wood's 1-7 descriptive anchors with 'All ratings were made using 5-point Likert scales, ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree)', which is what option_text carries, in English for the same reason as the items. resp 2, 3 and 4 are left BLANK because the paper labels only the two endpoints. instructions is blank: the paper reproduces no instruction text, only that participants completed the questionnaires in the classroom, and the canonical Wood instruction does not apply to a 5-point agreement administration. (4) mapping_basis=reconstructed. data/wang_2016_authenticity_relationship.py renames the source columns A_Living1/A_Living2/A_Living3/A_L4 -> authliving1..4, a number-preserving rename, so the code names the SUBSCALE at the source ('A_Living'); but the source carries no text, so WHICH of AS items 1/8/9/11 each number is comes from the canonical subscale numbering, not from any label. That inference is not verifiable against this dataset -- see verification status PARTIAL. (5) Verified (verify_wang_2016_study1_authliving.R): summing the live authliving + authalien + authexternal tables per person reproduces Wang's Table 1 Authenticity M=42.49 SD=6.19 (published 42.49/6.18) and its r=.61 with the live self-esteem total M=38.34 SD=5.08 (published 38.34/5.08/.61), which pins the block and the coding direction: reversing the authliving block (6-x) would give a block mean of 8.38 instead of 15.62 and a 12-item total of 35.24. Within-block order is NOT pinned -- item-rest r of .442/.640/.478/.465 does not separate four positively keyed items, and the study publishes no per-item statistics. (6) Rights: no reserved right found and no register row covers this instrument. The Authenticity Scale is published in the appendix of Wood, Linley, Maltby, Baliousis & Joseph (2008), J Counseling Psychology 55(3):385-399, doi:10.1037/0022-0167.55.3.385; searches for a rights-holder terms page turned up no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause, and the reproductions located (cic.edu PDF, PMC7838489, scielo.isciii.es Brazilian/Portuguese validation) carry no use restriction beyond the APA article's own copyright notice, which is a notice about the article rather than a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case). Shipped under 'silence is permission'; no ship/ship_with_note register row was written, per the rule that a round may only write block rows.
public_note: Item text is shown in English: Wang (2016) administered a Chinese translation of the Authenticity Scale and no Chinese wording is published in the PLOS deposit (the SPSS file carries no variable or value labels), so Wood et al.'s (2008) original English for Authentic Living items 1, 8, 9 and 11 ships instead, with the study's own 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree) anchors in place of Wood's 1-7 anchors. Which of those four canonical items each code authliving1-4 refers to is inferred from the standard subscale numbering and could not be checked against the data -- the block as a whole is verified (the three authenticity tables sum to the paper's published total of 42.49, SD 6.18), but a permutation within the four items would not be detectable.
